meanings.note: Between の and な (あなたのような人), describes someone or something 'like ...'.

examples.text: 春のような暖かい日です。
examples.trans: It is a warm day like spring.

examples.text: あなたのような人を探していました。
examples.trans: I was looking for someone like you.

meanings.en: come; go do something and return (after て-form)
meanings.note: Written in kana after a て-form (話してきます), expresses stepping away to do an action and coming back.

examples.text: ちょっと水を買ってきます。
examples.trans: I will go buy some water and be right back.

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').
Blunt or rowdy second-person pronoun used with subordinates, rivals, or close crew.

examples.trans: I leave it to you guys.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.

examples.text: よう、やっぱすぐ出てきたな。お前に報告があるんだよ。
examples.trans: Hey, knew you would get out fast. I have news to share with you.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.en: exist; be available; remain in place
meanings.note: Used for inanimate things and abstract concepts; after て-form (書いてある, 置いてある) describes a resulting state left in place.

examples.text: 名前が書いてあります。
お前ら、観光じゃないんだからしっかりしろよ。
examples.trans: Hey, this isn't sightseeing, so pull yourselves together.

examples.text: 彼女は来るんだろうな？
ちゃんとキャストはそろってるんだろうな？
examples.trans: You've got the whole cast properly lined up, right?

meanings.note: Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.
Casual, blunt contraction of あなた used between intimates or in heated speech.
Used among friends and peers by men; switch to 私 or 僕 in formal settings.
Replaces は, が, or を to add 'also' or 'too'.

examples.trans: Please give me this one too.

examples.text: あそこも新しい店です。
examples.trans: Over there is a new shop too.

meanings.note: In もういい, means 'already enough' or 'ready now'.
Read なん before だ/です/の, and なに before が/を or alone.

examples.text: 何を買いにきましたか。
examples.trans: What did you come to buy?

meanings.note: Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

examples.text: 俺ももう何年かで定年だからな。
examples.trans: I hit mandatory retirement age in just a few years myself.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Standalone pronoun ('this'), unlike この which requires a noun.

examples.text: これで定年後もお前をとっちめることができるってわけさ。
examples.trans: That way I can keep cracking down on you even after I retire.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.

examples.text: 俺も金なんとか集めるからよ。もうちょっと明るくやろうや。
examples.trans: I'll scrape together some money too, so let's keep our spirits up.

examples.text: ああ。リスクもあるが、懸けてみるか、トシ。
examples.trans: Yeah. There's risk involved too, though—ready to take the gamble, Toshi?

examples.text: 強制送還の金がかかるだけで、何の見せしめにもならないだろ？
examples.trans: Deporting them just costs money and doesn't serve as an example to anyone, right?

meanings.note: Refers to facts, matters, or affairs rather than physical objects (もの).

examples.text: 仕事のことを話します。

できる.gloss: be built; open; be able to

meanings.en: come into existence; be completed; can do
meanings.note: With buildings or stores (店ができる), means a new shop has been built or opened.

examples.text: 駅前に新しいカフェができました。
examples.trans: A new café opened in front of the station.

examples.text: 日本語が少しできます。
examples.trans: I can speak a little Japanese.

meanings.note: All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.
Verbal noun; 説明する means 'to explain'.

examples.text: 詳しい説明をお願いします。

meanings.note: Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

meanings.en: know; find out; be aware of
meanings.note: Godan verb; state of knowing is 知っている.

examples.text: 彼の電話番号を知っていますか。
examples.trans: Do you know his phone number?

examples.text: 本当の理由を知りたい。
examples.trans: I want to know the real reason.

meanings.note: Conditional particle attached to the hypothetical (e) stem of verbs and adjectives.

examples.text: 練習すれば上手になります。
examples.trans: If you practice, you will get better.
If it's cheap, I'll buy it.

meanings.note: Godan verb.

examples.text: このペンを使ってもいいですか。
もっと英語を使いましょう。

meanings.note: Attached to surnames, given names, or company names to show everyday respect; never used for oneself.
Refers to the upcoming occasion or a recent/current occasion.

examples.text: 今度一緒に食事しましょう。
examples.trans: Let's have a meal together next time.

examples.text: 今度の休みはどこへ行きますか。
examples.trans: Where are you going on your next day off?

meanings.note: Used for social/work issues as well as test questions.

examples.text: それは大きな問題です。
特に問題はありません。

meanings.en: cause; bring about; wake someone up
meanings.note: Godan transitive verb; 騒ぎを起こす means 'cause a commotion'.

examples.text: 次に騒ぎを起こしたら追い出すぞ。
examples.trans: If you cause a commotion next time, I'll throw you out.

examples.text: 朝七時に起こしてください。
examples.trans: Please wake me up at 7 a.m.

meanings.note: Attaches to a past-stem verb form to set up a condition ('if a fire starts').

examples.text: 火事になったら大変です。
examples.trans: If a fire breaks out, it will be terrible.

examples.text: 家に帰ったら電話します。
examples.trans: I will call when I get home.

meanings.en: open a store; bring out; hand in
meanings.note: 店を出す means opening a branch; 出しやがって attaches tough-guy disdainful やがる.

examples.text: 駅前に新しい店を出します。
examples.trans: We open a new branch in front of the station.

examples.text: 書類を出してください。

meanings.note: Follows a clause to give a reason or reassuring explanation.

examples.trans: Because it is close, I walk.

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.

meanings.en: bring to a halt; shut off
meanings.note: Transitive verb for stopping a car, engine, or machine.

examples.text: ここに車を止めてください。
エンジンを止めました。

meanings.note: Polite/dialectal negative ending, especially in ～ません.
て-form 売って links 'sell' into the next action.
Transitive ichidan verb.

examples.text: 毎日運動を続けています。
三か月続けてみてください。
examples.trans: Please try keeping it up for three months.

meanings.note: In casual speech, それ plus は often fuses into そりゃ ('well, as for that / of course').
Ichidan verb; potential form 決められる means 'can decide'.

examples.text: まだ何も決めていません。
今決められないなら、後で考えましょう。
examples.trans: If you can't decide now, let's think about it later.

meanings.note: Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).
Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.
Noun form of 騒ぐ (make a fuss).

examples.trans: It turned into a big commotion.

examples.trans: I have something I want to say too.

meanings.note: Verbal noun; 約束する means 'to promise'.

examples.text: 約束の時間に遅れました。
examples.trans: I was late for the appointment time.

meanings.note: Contracts では; launches a decision ('well then') or opens casual farewell じゃあね.
